events.context: /demerzel audit level 1 (loop-state check): both state/loops/*.loop.json instances fail validation. Instances use loop_id/goal/repo/risk/governance_mode/status and an iterations[] shape of {iteration,timestamp,action,outcome,governance_decision}; schema requires id/risk_level/initiator/target_repo/worker/reviewer/current_iteration/convergence/outcome and iterations items {number,started_at,work_summary,review_decision,governance_check}. Schema has drifted from the real AFK-loop instances.

Reconciled logic/loop-state.schema.json to the operational contract already encoded in schemas/loop-state.schema.json -- the copy demerzel_kit enforces at write time (demerzel_kit.py SCHEMA_DIR -> schemas/, via run_afk_cycle.py kit.write_artifact). Both files now carry the identical TOP-LEVEL required set: loop_id, goal, repo, risk, governance_mode, status, iterations. Enums on risk, governance_mode and status match the operational copy. The de-required fields (worker, reviewer, current_iteration, convergence, outcome, rich per-iteration governance check) are REMOVED ENTIRELY (not retained as optional) and were never a real guarantee: no loop instance in repo history has ever carried them, no script reads them, and the prior required set was unsatisfiable regardless -- its target_repo enum was [ix, tars, ga] while both instances are repo=demerzel. All 2 state/loops/*.loop.json instances validate against BOTH schemas. This file remains MORE PERMISSIVE than the enforced copy one level down: schemas/ requires `outcome` in iterations.items and sets additionalProperties:false at both levels; this file does neither. Reintroducing the removed fields therefore requires changing schemas/loop-state.schema.json first. Issue #834 tracks enriching the emitter; note its acceptance criteria name this file, but the file governing writes is schemas/loop-state.schema.json. The duplication between the two copies is the root cause of this drift and is tracked separately.

effectiveness.proposition: logic/loop-state.schema.json accurately describes the autonomous-loop state instances it governs
